text.p: LJUBLJANA - Following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Slovenian newspapers:

- The centre-left Liberal Democrats of prime minister -designate Janez Drnovsek and the conservative People's Party signed a coalition agreement late on Monday to form a government with 19 cabinet posts.
- Slovenian and Croatian economic ministers agreed to form a committee to manage Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko, which is in mutual ownership.
- Slovenia has banned the import and transport of pigs and pork products from the Netherlands in order to avoid the spread of swine fever.

- The Christian Democrats and the Social Democrats, former partners of the People's Party in the "Spring" alliance, said the People's Party participation in the government was "immoral" as it caused a break-up of the alliance.
- Minister of Economic Relations and Development Janko Dezelak said government-controlled prices of electricity, petrol, medicines and insurance premiums will be raised just once in 1997.
